messages:
Devon: p95 for /v1/generate (redwood-v2-13b) jumped to ~480ms in us-west1 over the last 30m, looks tied to continuous batching hitting the configured max_batch of 32 :frowning:
Priya: which pool/tenant? dedicated or shared?
Devon: dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (tenant: search-prod). median seq ~64, request size distribution hasn't changed.
Marco: we rolled the q4 runtime patch last night that tightened max_batch enforcement. Could be a side effect.
Anya: can you dump the admission metrics? specifically `admitted`, `rejected`, `max_batch_inflight` over the last 1h?
Devon: paste from Grafana (trimmed):
```
sum(rate(runtime_batch_admit_total{pool="dedicated-gpu-pool-3"}[5m])) by (result) -> admitted=120rps, rejected=18rps
max_batch_inflight{pool="dedicated-gpu-pool-3"} -> median=32, 95p=32
runtime_request_latency_ms_p95{route="/v1/generate"} -> 480
```
Lee: 18rps rejection is high for a steady workload. That'll push more short-requests into tail backpressure and cause head-of-line waits.
Priya: is KV prefix caching working? If caching is hit rate dropped it could increase decode chunk sizes and push batches to max.
Devon: cache hit rate is stable. `kv_cache_hit_ratio=0.78` on that pool.
ops-joe: any network flaps or shard unevenness? We saw a couple of slot rebalances in us-west1 earlier.
Marco: yeah, autoscaler kicked a pod replacement at 04:12. There was a short period where one shard went to 0 capacity and others absorbed load.
Anya: That can create hot-shard queueing. If the admission control uses per-shard max_batch, the shards that stay up will hit 32 while others can't accept, creating queuing in the front-end.
sre-runbook-bot: Runbook step: if continuous max_batch saturation -> (1) enable soft_admit on pool, (2) temporarily allow burst_capacity=+20%, (3) monitor p95 for 15m.
Lee: quick mitigation: enable soft_admit for dedicated-gpu-pool-3 and raise burst_capacity to 20% for 10m. I'll flip it now.
Priya: note: soft_admit may increase per-request latency variance — we need to balance SLO drift vs tail.
Devon: Lee flipped soft_admit and +20% burst at 04:36. p95 dropped to 310ms within 3m, admitted rejects down to 3rps.
Marco: good. For a longer fix we should either: (A) increase reserved slots for pool-3, (B) lower max_batch to 24 and tune packing window, or (C) bias routing away from pool-3 when autoscaler is rebuilding.
Anya: lowering max_batch reduces throughput and increases cost unless we add capacity; might worsen queueing under bursty load.
Priya: can we try lowering the pack_window from 20ms -> 12ms for this pool to reduce waiting time? Might reduce average batch size without carving capacity.
sre-runbook-bot: Advisory: pack_window < 15ms can increase GPU kernel overhead for long sequences. Test on canary first.
Lee: I can deploy a canary with pack_window=12ms to pool-3 for 30m. If p95 stays <350 and throughput stays within 95% of baseline we can roll.
ops-joe: cost note: if we increase reserved capacity, budget impact ~+12% monthly for that fleet. Heads up to finance.
Devon: current status: soft_admit ON, burst +20% active, canary scheduled for 04:55. Will update after 30m. Thanks all :thumbsup:
